```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5)
```

## Why

Most papers that integrate binding data (ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN, ATAC-seq) with
expression show a few "representative" genome browser tracks. These are
usually picked by eye, and the choice is rarely reported. That makes the
examples hard to reproduce, and it lets avoidable artifacts into figures:

* a peak that the annotation assigns to a gene tens of kilobases away;
* a peak in a paralog cluster where reads cannot be placed uniquely;
* a peak in a gap of the signal track, so the browser shows nothing;
* gene symbols that differ between the annotation, the differential
  expression table and the gene models, so a gene silently drops out;
* a change in binding that looks specific to the example but is in fact
  genome-wide.

LocusPick turns the selection into an explicit pipeline. Every candidate and
every quality flag is kept in a table, and the ranking weights can be stated in
a figure legend.

## Workflow

```{r}
library(LocusPick)
ex <- locusPickExample()
```

The example is a synthetic 60 kb chromosome with six genes, eight peaks, two
signal tracks (`A` and `B`, think "young" and "old") and a mappability track.

### 1. Gene models and peaks

```{r}
ex$genes                     # readGeneModels("genes.gtf")
ex$peaks                     # asPeaks("peaks.bed")
```

`readGeneModels()` accepts a GTF/GFF path or an imported `GRanges`.
`asPeaks()` accepts BED/narrowPeak files, data frames or `GRanges`.

### 2. Gene groups from two contrasts

Groups combine regulation by the factor (from a perturbation such as a
knockout) with the direction of change in a condition (such as aging).

```{r}
de <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "toy_de.tsv", package = "LocusPick"))
ko  <- deTable(de, gene = "gene", lfc = "ko_lfc",   padj = "ko_padj")
age <- deTable(de, gene = "gene", lfc = "cond_lfc", padj = "cond_padj")
groups <- defineGroups(ko, age, alpha = 0.05, perturbationType = "loss",
                       conditionName = "condition")
groups
```

With `perturbationType = "loss"`, genes that go down in the knockout are
`activated` by the factor.

### 3. Candidates and quality control

```{r}
cand <- buildCandidates(ex$peaks, ex$genes, groups,
                        signal = ex$signal, mappability = ex$mappability,
                        maxDist = 5000, minMappability = 0.8, minCoverage = 0.5)
qcSummary(cand)
cand[, c("gene", "group", "peak_id", "feature", "A_mean", "B_mean",
         "mappability", "has_signal", "mappable", "eligible")]
```

Both *geneD* peaks fail, for different reasons: the promoter peak lies in a
low-mappability region, and the downstream peak sits in a gap of the signal
tracks. Both stay in the table, flagged, and *geneD*'s group has no eligible
example. That is itself worth knowing before choosing a figure panel.

If your peaks already carry a gene assignment (for example from HOMER or an
enhancer-target database), pass it with `geneCol`. LocusPick then checks each
assignment against your gene models instead of trusting it:

```{r}
pk <- ex$peaks
pk$gene <- c("geneA", "geneB", "geneA", "geneD", "geneE", "geneE", "geneF", "geneF")
chk <- checkAssignment(pk, ex$genes, geneCol = "gene")
chk[!chk$near_gene, ]
```

### 4. Ranking

`rankLoci()` scores eligible candidates within each group as a weighted mean of
percentile ranks. Positive weights reward high values and negative weights
reward low ones. A candidate missing any weighted value is not scored, so a
locus can never rank highly on a subset of the criteria.

```{r}
cand$loss <- cand$A_mean - cand$B_mean
ranked <- rankLoci(cand, c(A_mean = 1, loss = 1,
                           abs_lfc_perturbation = 1, abs_lfc_condition = 1))
top <- topLoci(ranked, n = 3)
top[, c("group", "gene", "peak_id", "score", "rank")]
```

Different groups can use different criteria by passing a named list of weight
vectors.

### 5. Is the change specific?

Before claiming that loss of binding at an example explains its expression
change, check whether the loss is specific to that group or seen at all peaks:

```{r}
signalShift(cand, "A_mean", "B_mean",
            background = signalAtPeaks(ex$peaks, ex$signal))
```

If every group and the background show a similar shift, a track showing reduced
binding at the example is consistent with the hypothesis but not specific to
it. That difference should be reflected in the figure legend.

### 6. Plots

```{r}
plotLocus(top[1, ], ex$signal, ex$genes,
          trackGroups = list(Binding = c("A", "B")),
          colors = c(A = "steelblue", B = "salmon"),
          expression = ex$expression)
```

Tracks in one `trackGroups` panel share a y-axis, so conditions are directly
comparable; different panels (for example CUT&RUN and ATAC) get their own
scales. For figure panels use `annotate = FALSE`, and set `yLimits` so several
loci share the same axes.

`reportLoci()` writes one page per locus, plus the full candidate table, for
review:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
reportLoci(top, "candidates.pdf", signal = ex$signal, genes = ex$genes,
           trackGroups = list(Binding = c("A", "B")),
           expression = ex$expression, candidates = ranked)
```

## Using your own data

For step-by-step options to produce each input (bigWigs from BAM or
bedGraph, consensus peaks, gene models, DE tables from DESeq2/edgeR/limma,
expression insets, mappability) and to check them with `checkInputs()`, see
`vignette("preparing-inputs", package = "LocusPick")`.

### Signal

Any of these can be used as a track:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
signal <- list(
    CNR_young = bigWigSource("cnr_young.bw"),          # bigWig file or URL
    CNR_old   = "cnr_old.bw",                          # a path also works
    ATAC      = rangesSource(rtracklayer::import("atac.bedGraph")),
    H3K27ac   = chromDictSource(readRDS("h3k27ac.rds"), binSize = 20),
    custom    = functionSource(function(chr, start, end) myFetcher(chr, start, end))
)
```

### Mappability

Umap multi-read mappability (Karimzadeh et al. 2018) gives, for each base,
the fraction of overlapping k-mers that map uniquely. The Umap authors
distribute it as a bedGraph; the bundled script converts it to an indexed
bigWig once:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
system.file("scripts", "make_umap_bw.sh", package = "LocusPick")
# bash make_umap_bw.sh 50      # k = read length closest to your data
```

Choose `k` close to your read length; shorter k is more conservative.

### Gene symbols

When sources come from different annotation releases, harmonize symbols
before building groups and gene models:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
h <- function(s) harmonizeSymbols(s, org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db)
genes <- readGeneModels("mm10.gtf", harmonize = h)
ko$gene  <- h(ko$gene)
age$gene <- h(age$gene)
```

## A complete example

The workflow below reproduces a CUT&RUN analysis of a liver transcription factor
in young and old mice, with a hepatocyte knockout as the perturbation:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
h <- function(s) harmonizeSymbols(s, org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db)
genes <- readGeneModels("mm10.gtf", harmonize = h)

ko  <- deTable(read.delim("ko_vs_control.tsv"), gene = "Gene",
               lfc = "log2FC", padj = "FDR")
age <- deTable(read.delim("old_vs_young.tsv"), gene = "Gene",
               lfc = "log2FoldChange", padj = "padj")
ko$gene <- h(ko$gene); age$gene <- h(age$gene)
groups <- defineGroups(ko, age, conditionName = "age")

signal <- list(CNR_young = "cnr_young.bw", CNR_old = "cnr_old.bw",
               ATAC_young = "atac_young.bw", ATAC_old = "atac_old.bw")
cand <- buildCandidates("young_consensus_peaks.bed", genes, groups,
                        signal = signal,
                        mappability = "k50.Umap.MultiTrackMappability.bw",
                        requireSignal = c("CNR_young", "CNR_old"))
qcSummary(cand)

cand$CNR_loss <- cand$CNR_young_mean - cand$CNR_old_mean
w <- c(CNR_young_mean = 1, CNR_loss = 1,
       abs_lfc_perturbation = 1, abs_lfc_condition = 1)
ranked <- rankLoci(cand, w)
signalShift(ranked, "CNR_young_mean", "CNR_old_mean",
            background = signalAtPeaks("young_consensus_peaks.bed", signal[1:2]))

reportLoci(topLoci(ranked, n = 10), "review.pdf", signal = signal, genes = genes,
           trackGroups = list(`CUT&RUN` = c("CNR_young", "CNR_old"),
                              ATAC = c("ATAC_young", "ATAC_old")),
           candidates = ranked)
```

## Reporting

A sentence like the following lets readers reproduce the choice:

> Representative loci were selected with LocusPick (v`r packageVersion("LocusPick")`).
> Peaks were assigned to the nearest gene within 5 kb; loci with mean Umap k50
> mappability < 0.8, < 50% signal coverage, or an assignment inconsistent with
> the gene models were excluded. Remaining loci were ranked within each group by
> the mean percentile rank of young CUT&RUN signal, loss of signal with age, and
> the absolute knockout and age log2 fold changes. The top-ranked locus per
> group is shown; all candidates are listed in Supplementary Table X.

```{r}
sessionInfo()
```
